outcomes: A Kubernetes probe or an uptime check reads any Putnami workload with the same paths and status codes
Liveness never fails during startup or shutdown, so an orchestrator does not restart a healthy workload
An operator reads a failing probe's own error message in the readiness envelope
nonGoals: A /metrics scrape endpoint: telemetry is pushed, as ADR 0001 records
Authentication of the operational endpoints, which workloads put behind an admin port or a sidecar
A JSON Schema for the envelope: the Go types, the strict validator and the shared fixtures are the contract
The TypeScript platform() plugin of @putnami/application, which reads the same fixtures under its own tests

requirements.text: ProtocolVersion is 1, and a test pins it, so a change to the endpoint paths, the envelope, the status-code rules or the probe semantics is a reviewed version bump.

The canonical paths are /livez, /healthz, /readyz and /version, served with GET. /healthz and /readyz aggregate probes and report unavailable until the workload starts; /livez and /version do neither. /debug/pprof/ is the one opt-in endpoint, and an unknown endpoint kind resolves to nothing.
The contract declares /debug/pprof/ opt-in only, so a runtime leaves it off unless the workload enables it. Its sub-paths are the index, /cmdline, /profile, /symbol, /trace and /{name}.

An envelope status is ok, unavailable or degraded. ok requires every checks entry to be exactly ok, degraded requires at least one failing entry, and unavailable carries no checks. A probe name matches [a-z0-9][a-z0-9_./-]{0,63}. Every valid envelope fixture validates, every invalid one is refused, and the envelopes the Go runtime serves validate.

ok maps to HTTP 200, and unavailable and degraded map to 503. No other status maps to a code. The Go runtime answers /healthz with the code of its envelope status before start, while running and when a probe fails.

Probes are discovered from the module tree and keyed by plugin name, and an explicit registration wins over a discovered probe. A health probe feeds /healthz and a readiness probe feeds /readyz, each with a stated failure consequence. A probe is concurrency-safe, respects cancellation and gets 5 seconds by default, and its failure is reported as its error string.

A mount prefix drops ASCII whitespace and slashes at both ends and gains one leading slash, so an empty, / or // prefix becomes empty and /admin/ becomes /admin, while an interior doubled slash is kept. Joining a prefix and an endpoint path yields one canonical path, and the Go runtime serves its endpoints only under it.

The strict validators register exactly nine platform.* codes. platform.missing_probe names a required probe that is absent; it is reported through a degraded envelope, so it is not a validator code and needs no version bump.
